name: Stack Trace Analysis Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on stack trace analysis so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on stack trace analysis so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to stack trace analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When stack trace analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Keep stack trace analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen stack trace analysis approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Check that stack trace analysis terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. Keep stack trace analysis outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Prefer explicit, readable stack trace analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. When multiple stack trace analysis strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. State assumptions about stack trace analysis explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Before starting stack trace analysis work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new stack trace analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop stack trace analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated stack trace analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of stack trace analysis correctness.
- Do not skip documenting stack trace analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about stack trace analysis over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
